title: Tell parties apart by name, place and shape, with no red and blue.
rule: Rule 01.2 draws every party in one neutral ink with its name on the mark, and Rule 01.1 keeps red off every party. A chart then tells parties apart by what a reader can read without color: the name on or beside each mark, the mark’s place in the order or in its party’s own panel, a solid and an open mark where two sides sit side by side, and a word or sign for direction, as in “Republican +2.2”.
No election graphic pairs red with blue, social cards included, and Prussian never stands for a party.

text: Red and blue turn a chart of results into team colors, and a reader decides which side the chart is on before reading a number. A name on each mark gives readers on both sides the same facts, in color or in grayscale.
why.basis: Design judgment, from the chart system our founder and editor approved in November 2026

builders: Party data takes the party role in any form; the kit fails a party mark in Pillar Red or Prussian.

specs.label: Party marks
specs.value: One neutral ink for every party, Charcoal on Newsprint

specs.label: Two sides at a glance
specs.value: One solid and one open mark, in the same ink (Rule 01.2)

specs.label: Direction
specs.value: An arrow, the mark’s place or a printed lead, such as “Republican +2.2”

specs.label: Seats on a map
specs.value: One panel for each party, named with the seats it won, each seat filled in its winner’s panel and its margin in gray steps (Rule 14.5)

specs.label: Never
specs.value: Red against blue, or Prussian for a party

correct.caption: Every party takes the same ink and its name, so the bars compare seats and nothing else.
correct.alt: Bars in one ink with each party named on its bar. Republicans held 218 House seats and Democrats 214 on November 11, 2026, with one independent and two seats empty.

failure.caption: Fails Rule 14.7. Red and blue stand for the parties and a key holds their initials, so the chart reads as one team against another and loses the parties in grayscale.
failure.alt: Failure case: do not publish. Two bars, a red one marked R at 218 and a blue one marked D at 214, with a key of a red square for R and a blue square for D.
